children: Australian interest rates have probably peaked but investors shouldn't rush to pivot just yet, UBS strategists warn. The investment bank's economists are confident that Australia's cash rate has peaked at an 18-year-high 4.85%, and have pulled forward their target for the first cut by three months to August 2027. However, their strategy counterparts see growing risk of more significant earnings downgrades by domestic companies. They acknowledge that buying cyclical consumer and housing stocks may look tempting, but warn in a note that the unemployment rate is rising and that this has long been associated with a loss of earnings momentum. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
